approval.cost: No fee mentioned in the docs read
approval.trigger: No review before real users can connect, and no marketplace approval for user OAuth2 apps or public bots. Instead, two scale gates: (1) App Verification is 'required for your app to scale past 100 servers' (verified bots have no maximum number of guilds); it requires the development team's owner to verify identity through Stripe, and Discord may ask you to periodically reverify. (2) Privileged Intent review: since June 10, 2026 the threshold is users, not servers; if unique users who can see your app exceed 10,000, you must apply per intent with a use-case justification, within a 90-day window, and reapply annually.
approval.wait: Verification and intent review durations are not published; the stated figures are the 90-day application windows and the annual reapplication cadence

blockers.detail: An unverified bot stops growing at 100 servers. Clearing the wall is not an app-quality review: the owner of the development team that owns the app must verify their identity through Stripe, and Discord may require periodic reverification.
blockers.howToClear: Complete App Verification from the portal's App Verification tab before your growth hits the cap.
blockers.title: The 100-server wall for unverified bots

blockers.detail: Guild Presences, Guild Members, and Message Content can be toggled freely below the threshold; past 10,000 unique users you must apply for each with a justification, and denial is a stated outcome where interactions can do the job (Discord's posture: deny Message Content when slash commands/components suffice). Access must be reapplied for annually.
blockers.howToClear: Design to avoid privileged intents (interactions over message reading) where possible; where genuinely needed, write specific per-intent use cases.
blockers.title: Privileged Intent review (Message Content above all)

blockers.detail: Scopes like applications.builds.upload, dm_channels.read, identify.premium, rpc, and voice are 'only available to approved partners'; relationships.read requires applying via the Social SDK. The docs warn that requesting scopes 'without approval from Discord may cause errors or undocumented behavior in the OAuth2 flow'.
blockers.howToClear: Stick to the public scope set unless you have partner approval in hand.
blockers.title: Partner-gated scopes error out

alternatives: Bot install (scope 'bot', usually with applications.commands): a callback-less flow authorized by a server admin; the bot then acts with its own bot token and guild permissions, independent of any user
User install (integration_type=1 with applications.commands): installs to a user's account and works across their DMs and servers
Client credentials grant: a bearer token for the app owner's own resources (e.g. applications.commands.update) and testing
flavor.recommended: An Application in the Discord Developer Portal, using the user OAuth2 authorization code grant
flavor.why: One Application bundles the OAuth2 client (client ID + secret), an automatically attached bot user, and installation settings. For a SaaS whose users connect their own accounts, the code grant (scopes like identify, email, guilds, guilds.members.read) returns a bearer token plus refresh token acting as that user. Choose the bot flavor only if the product lives inside Discord servers, remembering it is authorized by a server admin, not by each end user.

Write per-intent use-case justifications if you cross the privileged-intent threshold
name: Discord
nuances: The bot flow shape-shifts: request any scope beyond bot/applications.commands and it converts into a full authorization code grant (response_type mandatory, redirect to your first registered URI). Enabling 'Require OAuth2 Code Grant' forces this for everyone.
Privileged Intents are a two-place switch: enable in the portal AND request in code, or the Gateway connection fails with DisallowedIntents. Changes take effect only on a new Gateway connection.

The implicit grant returns no refresh token (users re-authorize at expiry); prompt=none can skip re-consent for previously authorized scopes, but passthrough scopes like bot and webhook.incoming always require authorization.
For bots with elevated permissions, Discord enforces two-factor authentication on the owner's account when the bot is added to guilds with server-wide 2FA enabled.
Discord's authorize response includes an iss parameter per RFC 9207.
prerequisites: Your install-context and default scope/permissions decisions
For scale: the team owner's ability to complete Stripe identity verification

steps.detail: Developer Portal (discord.com/developers/applications) > New Application; set name and description. One Application bundles the OAuth2 client, a bot user, and installation settings.
steps.title: Create the Application

steps.detail: On the OAuth2 page, register your redirect URIs (the runtime redirect_uri must be one of them) and note the client ID and client secret. The portal's OAuth2 URL Generator helps build test links.
steps.title: Register redirect URIs; note credentials

steps.detail: On the Installation page, configure default install settings (install contexts: guild and/or user; default scopes and permissions). An authorize URL carrying only client_id uses these defaults. On the Bot page (if using a bot): retrieve/reset the bot token, set Public Bot, Require OAuth2 Code Grant, and any Privileged Gateway Intents.
steps.title: Configure installation defaults (and bot settings)

steps.detail: Build the authorize URL (with state), exchange the returned code at the token endpoint, refresh with grant_type=refresh_token, and revoke via the revocation endpoint. Individuals consent to user scopes; a server admin adds the bot via its invite URL.
steps.title: Implement the flows

steps.detail: Before you hit 100 servers, complete the App Verification checklist in the portal; the team owner verifies identity through Stripe. If unique users who can see your app pass 10,000, apply for each Privileged Intent with its use-case justification within the 90-day window, and calendar the annual reapplication.
